title: Impact of Intraoperative Fluid Therapy on the Survival of Microvascular Transplants in the Head and Neck Region
summary: This study analyzes existing medical records from patients who underwent microvascular tissue reconstruction in the head and neck region. The aim is to determine whether the amount and type of fluids given during surgery influence healing and postoperative complications. No additional tests or patient contacts are required; all data come from routine clinical documentation.
conditions: Microvascular Rekonstruktion with free tissue transfer
Malignant neoplasm: Lateral floor of mouth

interventions.name: This is a retrospective, single-center analysis of routine clinical data. All patients who have undergone microvascular free flap reconstruction in the head and neck region at the University Medical Center Mainz since 2018 will be consecutively included based on existing medical records. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients who underwent a microvascular free flap reconstruction in the head and neck region at the Department of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery, University Medical Center Mainz between October 2018 and August 2025.
- Availability of complete and relevant routine clinical data, including anesthesia records, operative reports, and postoperative documentation necessary for analysis.
- Microvascular free flap procedure performed for reconstructive purposes, such as fibular, radial forearm, anterolateral thigh (ALT), or other established free flap types.
- Age ≥ 18 years at the time of surgery.
- Elective or standard-of-care reconstructive procedure with documented intraoperative volume therapy parameters (i.e., excluding emergency cases without adequate documentation).
Exclusion criteria:
- Incomplete or missing routine clinical data, particularly insufficient documentation of intraoperative fluid therapy or hemodynamic parameters.
- Patients younger than 18 years at the time of surgery.
- Non-microvascular reconstructive procedures (e.g., local flaps, pedicled regional flaps).
- Reconstructions performed outside the head and neck region, even if microvascular.
